material_passport.source: PROTOCOL.md and 30 frozen structured contexts; five simulated patients, no human participants
material_passport.scope: Nine positive-history fields in four categories; identity and absent-surname controls excluded
material_passport.review_execution: Codex automated audit in delegated context; not a human assessment

method.semantic_grouping: Every prompt and selected-evidence file was read. Exact selected quote, header metadata and fact entity/attribute/value/status/current were checked against each rendered block. The 30 ARM_CONTEXT sections reduce to 10 exact text groups after replacing only session and turn numbers. Field judgments apply to each of the 30 contexts and have exact delivered blocks attached.
method.excluded_metadata: search_text, previous_value, previous_values, supersedes IDs and any unrendered JSON metadata were not counted as delivered support. Original turn IDs are locators only.
method.case_check: No positive-history gold value appears in CASE in any of the 30 prompts.
method.noninference_boundary: Absent delivered support is not absence from the persistent archive. Counts describe delivery only; they do not measure generated-answer accuracy or full-application performance.
method.position_and_sample_dependence: Three placements share the same semantic evidence within each profile and size; 270 field-context instances and 30 contexts are dependent observations from five simulated profiles. No significance test or independent-binomial interval is warranted.
method.semantic_content_delivery_definition: The actual rendered quote/value explicitly contains the correct gold value and requested basic relationship/status, regardless of speaker. This measures textual content availability, not confirmation, truth, answer correctness or full-app retention. Correct content inside patient proposed phrasing is counted as semantic content, with its hypothetical/proposed modality preserved. Incomplete values, unresolved agreement questions and cross-event relation inference do not satisfy this definition.
method.therapist_authoritative_subset_definitio: Conservative separate subset requiring full correct value and requested relationship/status in a rendered therapist utterance or therapist-sourced fact/source quote. This is not imposed on answer scoring and does not make patient-only content absent.
method.patient_text_detail: Plain patient recall with full correct value/relation is distinct from correct content embedded in proposed patient phrasing. Neither alone is therapist confirmation. Both remain visible along with competing values and incomplete relations.

support_class_legend.therapist_authoritative: Explicit semantic content with a delivered therapist record.
support_class_legend.non_authoritative_explicit: Explicit correct semantic content in patient recall or proposed wording; see confirmation_and_modality.
support_class_legend.partial_non_authoritative: Patient text includes only part of the full requested content or leaves agreement unresolved.
support_class_legend.partial_authoritative: Therapist content names a correct value but omits the requested cross-event relation.
support_class_legend.obsolete_non_authoritative: Patient text gives an obsolete value without its former/replaced status.
support_class_legend.absent_with_competing_patient_value: Correct target absent; patient text gives a competing value.

notable_cautions: No current appointment, former appointment, or unagreed appointment proposal field has its full value plus requested status explicitly delivered. Notebook and appointment partner content occur only in Daniel 64k patient recall; those fields lack therapist-authoritative support.
Rina Holt appears authoritatively in Juanita 64k only as a completed-activity coparticipant; counting appointment partner would require a cross-event inference.

Daniel 64k contains patient-only Tern Window and Rina Holt mentions and an obsolete Wednesday 17:45 arrangement without its replacement; all six Daniel contexts include patient references to Erik in the practice venue examples.

All six Jason contexts contain the correct venue relation inside patient proposed phrasing, without a therapist utterance. This counts as explicit semantic content delivery while remaining unconfirmed by therapist evidence.
Patient facts marked proposed/current or proposed/superseded are about proposed statements or phrasing; those tags do not establish the status of the embedded appointment or venue.
Retrieval budgets, complete-archive access, query truncation, and the component-only scope remain as described in PROTOCOL.md. This audit did not alter any input or inspect generated answers.
